Listen to this article Share Ericsson, a global telecommunications and networking technology company, has marked its 150th anniversary with a celebration in Lagos, highlighting its contributions to Nigeria’s telecommunications development and outlining its commitment to the country’s digital future. The event brought together customers, employees, government representatives, partners and other stakeholders to commemorate the company’s 150 years of innovation in communications and connectivity. Founded in 1876, Ericsson has evolved from developing early telecommunications technologies to providing mobile network infrastructure and digital solutions that support businesses, individuals and societies globally. In Nigeria, the company has maintained a presence since 1978, supporting telecommunications network deployments. One of its major milestones in the country was its contribution to the launch of Nigeria’s first GSM network in 2001, which marked a significant shift in the country’s mobile communications landscape. The company’s involvement in Nigeria’s telecommunications industry has continued with the introduction of newer technologies, including support for the launch of 5G services in 2022. In 2024, Ericsson and the Federal Government signed a cooperation framework covering 5G technology development, deployment and innovation, as well as knowledge exchange, capacity building and digital skills development. Speaking at the anniversary celebration, Majda Lahlou Kassi, Vice President and Head of Ericsson West and Southern Africa, said the company remained committed to supporting Nigeria’s digital transformation. She said Nigeria was a crucial market on the African continent, expressing confidence in its potential and the opportunities for further development of its digital economy. “As we celebrate 150 years of Ericsson, we are not only reflecting on our past; we are looking ahead to Nigeria’s future. Nigeria is a crucial market on the African continent, and we believe in its potential,” she said. Kassi added that Ericsson looked forward to working with customers, partners and other stakeholders to help shape the country’s digital future. The company also highlighted artificial intelligence (AI), automation and autonomous networks as key areas expected to shape the next phase of telecommunications development. It noted that rising mobile data consumption and increasingly sophisticated digital services would require high-performing and programmable networks to support enterprise innovation, improve connectivity experiences and unlock new opportunities associated with AI. Ericsson said it would continue collaborating with Nigeria’s telecommunications ecosystem to strengthen digital infrastructure and support the country’s broader digital transformation ambitions. Joshua Bassey SENIOR ANALYST - LABOUR/LAGOS STATE
